source.title: Orienting attention based on long-term memory experience

confidence_rationale: Direct human evidence that a hippocampus-dependent memory signal steers spatial attention (a sampling allocation) and that hippocampal activity tracks the behavioural benefit. Supports the propagation half of MECH-082 (stored map content -> perceptual sampling bias without sensory relearning). It does not test map DISTORTION, the E2 intermediary, or causality (fMRI correlation), so mapping fidelity caps confidence.
failure_signatures: Hippocampal engagement is correlational (event-related fMRI); the paper cannot rule out that hippocampal activity is a by-product of retrieval that runs in parallel with, rather than upstream of, the frontoparietal orienting signal.

Memories here are ACCURATE (learned target locations); the paper says nothing about whether an erroneous or distorted memory would bias sampling in the same way, which is the load-bearing half of MECH-082.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Stable long-term memories of object locations within naturalistic scenes guide spatial orienting within short intervals and improve detection; memory-guided orienting recruits the hippocampus together with the parietal-frontal orienting network, and hippocampal activity is specifically engaged by memory-guided (not cue-guided) orienting and correlates with the behavioural advantage.
mapping.ree_translation: Read as the biological precedent for the MECH-082 propagation path: map-derived expectations (hippocampal/E2-side content) bias where E1-level perceptual sampling is allocated, on a trial-by-trial timescale, with no retraining of the sensory encoder. The hippocampal-frontoparietal interaction is the nearest analogue to an E2-to-E1 sampling-control consumer.
mapping.mapping_caveat: REE's claim routes the bias through E2 predictions and the MECH-081 sufficiency constraint; the paper identifies a hippocampus + frontoparietal network, not a forward-model stage, so the E2 intermediary is an REE interpretation, not a finding. The memories were veridical; distortion-driven bias is not tested. Spatial orienting is one dimension of 'sampling allocation'; REE's per-dimension allocation DV is broader.
mapping.source_context: Healthy human adults, naturalistic-scene memory-guided vs. cue-guided spatial orienting task, event-related fMRI.

confidence_components.notes: Neuron, well-cited, replicated paradigm family (Nobre lab). Mapping capped by veridical-memory design and correlational hippocampal evidence.
